payload.title: Calculating Area and Perimeter of Polygons (notation reconstruction)
payload.subject: MATH
objectives: Calculate the area and perimeter of rectangles and triangles.
payload.body:
## 5. Worked Example 1 — The School Football Field

A rectangular football field at a school in Gbarnga is 90 meters long and 45 meters wide. To find the area we use the formula A_{\text{rectangle}} = l \times w. Substituting the values, A = 90 \times 45 = 4050 \text{ m}^2. The groundskeeper needs enough grass seed to cover 4050 square meters. To find how much rope is needed to go around the field, we calculate the perimeter using P_{\text{rectangle}} = 2(l + w). So P = 2(90 + 45) = 2 \times 135 = 270 \text{ m}. This means 270 meters of rope are needed, which is an important consideration when budgeting for school sports equipment and planning the maintenance of community facilities in Liberia.

## 6. Guided Practice

A classroom is 8 m long and 6 m wide. Find its area and perimeter using the formulas above.

## 7. Worked Example 2 — Triangular Garden Bed

The area of a triangle is found using \(A_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}bh\), where b is the base and h is the height. For a garden bed with a base of 10 m and a height of 12 m, A = \\frac{1}{2} \\times 10 \\times 12 = 60 \\text{ m}^2. The perimeter of the triangle is $P = a + b + c$, so with sides 13 m, 13 m and 10 m, $P = 13 + 13 + 10 = 36\text{ m}$. A trader who sells palm oil for L$500 a gallon might use these skills to plan a market stall.
